slides.visual_description: Module 1 Completion and Transition Prompt — Recognize that Module 1 is complete and orient to the transition from innovator mindset toward the learner's next leadership-identity journey.
slides.narration_text: Pause on the single message: the module you just completed set your innovator mindset. LEAD THE WAY isn’t a slogan—it’s your next posture. The work now is personal: how will you begin your leadership‑identity journey inside your own system? To guide that turn, we’ll briefly name the specific foundations you’ve already built, then step into the work of becoming the leader who can carry an opportunity forward.
slides.duration_rationale: Brief reflective close-and-turn with two visual anchors.
slides.narrative_arc: From Module 1 closure to readiness for Module 2 through a concise bridge that reframes completion as the start of a personal leadership journey
slides.script_notes: Module 1 Completion and Transition Prompt — Recognize that Module 1 is complete and orient to the transition from innovator mindset toward the learner's next leadership-identity journey.

slides.visual_description: What Module 1 Established — Recall the major mindset outcomes named in the close: mapping macro forces and populating the Opportunity Radar as prerequisites to the next module.
slides.narration_text: The main message: three foundations are in place. You mapped the larger forces shaping the health landscape. You populated your Opportunity Radar to identify real innovation targets. Taken together, your mindset is established—exactly the prerequisites for the leadership journey that follows.
slides.duration_rationale: Three concise recap beats confirmed against the summary card.
slides.narrative_arc: From completed mindset foundations to recognition of what has been prepared through a recap of macro forces, opportunity sensing, and system redesign readiness
slides.script_notes: What Module 1 Established — Recall the major mindset outcomes named in the close: mapping macro forces and populating the Opportunity Radar as prerequisites to the next module.

slides.display_title: Recap Beat: From Macro Forces to Opportunity Radar
slides.visual_description: Recap Beat: From Macro Forces to Opportunity Radar — Understand that the learner's mindset work in Module 1 included both seeing larger system forces and identifying innovation targets through the Opportunity Radar.
slides.narration_text: Think of your gains along two dimensions. First, seeing the system: noticing structural, economic, and social currents—macro forces shaping care from the outside in. Then, targeting the opportunity: translating that awareness into concrete innovation targets; the Opportunity Radar turned perception into possibility.
slides.duration_rationale: Two-dimension recap with brief visual context reference.
slides.narrative_arc: From completed mindset foundations to recognition of what has been prepared through a recap of macro forces, opportunity sensing, and system redesign readiness
slides.script_notes: Recap Beat: From Macro Forces to Opportunity Radar — Understand that the learner's mindset work in Module 1 included both seeing larger system forces and identifying innovation targets through the Opportunity Radar.

slides.display_title: Recap Beat: From Reaction to Redesign
slides.visual_description: Recap Beat: From Reaction to Redesign — Understand the closing reframing that the learner is moving from reacting to the health system toward redesigning it.
slides.narration_text: Here’s the reframing: reaction versus redesign. Reaction is living at the mercy of pressures and disruptions; redesign is acting with intention to shape the system. By contrast with reacting, redesign is the identity you’re stepping into. With that readiness in place, it’s time to face a hard truth about innovation: ideas don’t move themselves—leaders move them. Next, we’ll name what it actually takes to carry an opportunity through a complex health system.
slides.duration_rationale: Short contrast plus a two‑part seam into the hinge cluster.
slides.narrative_arc: From completed mindset foundations to recognition of what has been prepared through a recap of macro forces, opportunity sensing, and system redesign readiness
slides.script_notes: Recap Beat: From Reaction to Redesign — Understand the closing reframing that the learner is moving from reacting to the health system toward redesigning it.

slides.display_title: Why Ideas Alone Are Not Enough
slides.visual_description: Why Ideas Alone Are Not Enough — Understand the source claim that idea quality is insufficient without the leader who can champion the opportunity inside a complex health system.
slides.narration_text: A blunt truth: a brilliant idea without a capable champion is just a hypothesis waiting to expire. In a matrixed health system, the strength of an innovation concept is only one variable; the rest is human—navigating politics, building coalitions, and sustaining momentum. The idea needs a carrier, and that carrier is you.
slides.duration_rationale: Quote plus explanatory contrast requires fuller delivery.
slides.narrative_arc: From confidence in the idea to recognition of leadership as the decisive factor through contrast between opportunity value and the capacity to champion it in a matrixed health system
slides.script_notes: Why Ideas Alone Are Not Enough — Understand the source claim that idea quality is insufficient without the leader who can champion the opportunity inside a complex health system.

slides.visual_description: Tension Beat: The Idea-Leader Gap — Recognize the challenge that a viable opportunity can still fail if the leader cannot carry it through a matrixed health system.
slides.narration_text: Here’s the turn. The opportunity is real and addressable—urgent, even. Yet the system is complex, crowded with stakeholders, competing priorities, and structural friction. Without someone equipped to navigate, persuade, and persist, progress stalls. Viability alone does not guarantee movement.
slides.duration_rationale: Three-card tension build with explicit turn language.
slides.narrative_arc: From confidence in the idea to recognition of leadership as the decisive factor through contrast between opportunity value and the capacity to champion it in a matrixed health system
slides.script_notes: Tension Beat: The Idea-Leader Gap — Recognize the challenge that a viable opportunity can still fail if the leader cannot carry it through a matrixed health system.

slides.display_title: Develop Beat: The Leadership Capacities Required
slides.visual_description: Develop Beat: The Leadership Capacities Required — Identify the specific capacities named in the source as necessary for success: political savvy, communication skills, and leadership identity.
slides.narration_text: What closes that gap are specific capacities. Political savvy: navigating systems, relationships, and power dynamics with awareness and intention. Communication skills: articulating a clear, persuasive vision that moves people and organizations. And leadership identity: owning who you are as a leader—the foundation all the others grow from.
slides.duration_rationale: Names and defines three capacities without over-teaching.
slides.narrative_arc: From confidence in the idea to recognition of leadership as the decisive factor through contrast between opportunity value and the capacity to champion it in a matrixed health system
slides.script_notes: Develop Beat: The Leadership Capacities Required — Identify the specific capacities named in the source as necessary for success: political savvy, communication skills, and leadership identity.

slides.display_title: Resolve Beat: Leadership as the Next Build
slides.visual_description: Resolve Beat: Leadership as the Next Build — Accept that the next step after mindset is to build the leader capable of solving the waiting clinical problem.
slides.narration_text: First, mindset built the base—you mapped forces and worked your Opportunity Radar. That feeds the next build: your leadership identity to champion an opportunity. Then the work produces momentum—the clinical problem is waiting, and the next build is the leader. The mindset is the foundation; the leader is the structure raised on it. With that hinge set, let’s preview the identity work you’ll take on next.
slides.duration_rationale: Order-dependent hinge with diagram walkthrough and takeaway.
slides.narrative_arc: From confidence in the idea to recognition of leadership as the decisive factor through contrast between opportunity value and the capacity to champion it in a matrixed health system
slides.script_notes: Resolve Beat: Leadership as the Next Build — Accept that the next step after mindset is to build the leader capable of solving the waiting clinical problem.

slides.display_title: Preview of Module 2: From Mindset to Identity
slides.visual_description: Preview of Module 2: From Mindset to Identity — Preview that Module 2 will focus on defining leadership identity, communicating vision, and inspiring others to join the cause.
slides.narration_text: Now we move from mindset to identity. First, define your leadership identity—clarify who you are and what you stand for at your core. Then, communicate your vision so others can see it and believe in it. Finally, inspire others to join—turn a mindset into a movement around a shared cause. The opening module is complete; it’s time to step fully into your identity as a leader. See you in the next module.
slides.duration_rationale: Three-step preview with a concise farewell.
slides.narrative_arc: From bridge anticipation to clear next-step orientation through a concise preview of Module 2 leadership identity work
slides.script_notes: Preview of Module 2: From Mindset to Identity — Preview that Module 2 will focus on defining leadership identity, communicating vision, and inspiring others to join the cause.
